claim: From Epoch's data: the released record rose 38.89 points in the two years to 18 Nov 2026 (19.4 a year; 17.8 then 21.1); a straight-line fit through record-setters gives about 16.9 a year; the record's pace was about 15-16 a year from Sep 2024 to Oct 2025 and about 19-21 since, roughly 1.3x.

The most capable unreleased system is about 3 months (80% range 1-7) ahead of the released frontier, about 5 points, based on METR's 2-month measurement in early 2026, longer holding at Anthropic, OpenAI's withheld model, and the fact that two leading releases came within the last 9 days.

Translation rule: about 6 ECI points per doubling of the 50% time horizon up to week-scale tasks (16.6-21 points a year divided by about 3-4 doublings a year), rising to 10-15 points per doubling beyond month-scale tasks; scores above about 400 are a convention for much faster progress.

The FactSet (July) and S&P-sourced (Aug, reported Nov) capex projections are near-simultaneous estimates with different coverage, not a revision; 2027-28 compute is therefore mostly but not wholly funded, and the financial downside falls mainly on 2029-31.
Weighting METR's 1.9x finding against public-data estimates (0.99-1.4x), the public record's own speed-up (about 1.3x) and Anthropic's labour-to-output view, current acceleration is about 1.3-1.45x.

Starting from about 179: faster than 19.4 a year by end-2031 means above 278.5 (37th percentile, so P = 0.63); less than half means below 228.8 (about the 10th percentile, P = 0.10). For end-2028 the thresholds are 220.3 (P faster 0.65) and 199.7 (P below 0.06).

Today's best systems likely reach a 50% time horizon of roughly one to two working weeks on well-defined software tasks: METR measured about 12 hours in Feb-Mar 2026 when the record was about 160-163, and the record has since risen about 11-14 points, about two doublings.

Lower tail: a multi-year pause or court-ordered limits, a financial correction with negative cash flow, a chip-supply shock, or reinforcement-learning returns flattening could together hold the pace near or below the pre-reasoning 8 points a year; I judge results below about 203 at end-2031 to be about 1 in 100.

Upper tail: compounding AI-driven acceleration with returns to research above 1 could raise the pace several-fold by 2029-30; the 95th (530) and 99th (760) percentiles correspond to average paces of about 69 and 114 points a year from today.
